summary: New sense 2: (Part act., von einer Frau) schwanger;

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 3.4/19)

data.turoyo: <...> omər maxlaṣxuli i kačkaṯe ʕomər baytayxu. <...>
data.translation: <...> Er sagte: Ihr habt mir dieses Mädchen gerettet, dafür sei euch gedankt. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum sense-1 cell; explicit reason for thanks and plural possessors.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (63/49)

data.turoyo: Mhalaxli məqdar d fəlga d saʕaye bu ṭurano, maṭino l dawmo, l ṭaraşto, d kətyo ʕamərto, ḥəlli, ḥzeli bəḥto d ṭayro taḥt i dawmaṯe.
data.translation: Ich schritt etwa eine halbe Stunde auf jenem Gebirge vorwärts, da gelangte ich zu einem Baume, einer Steineiche mit Dichten Blättern, blickte hin und sah ein Vogelei unter jenem Baume liegen.

rationale: Better density context than isolated plant examples; referent is a leafy living tree.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (66/112)
rationale: Fills Infectum sense-1 cell to five; short optative God-house blessing, interpretable on its own.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (75/61)

data.turoyo: <...> Ono, babi mərleli: ʕamṯux, ṣaʕra ġalabe ʕamuro yo, w kobəʕ nošo mfalela! Aṯino d adyawma mfalenax! <...>
data.translation: <...> Mein Vater hat mir gesagt: Das Haar deiner Tante ist sehr dicht, jemand muss ihr die Läuse ablesen. So bin ich heute gekommen, um dich zu lausen. <...>

rationale: Participant extension to dense hair, with explicit degree and action motivated by density.

summary: example for sense 1b in Part act. (93/33)

data.turoyo: Me d yasəqno ʕal qarʕa d i=qalʕo, xurebəh kulle ʕatiqe w hən mənne ḥariwe w hən mənne ab=bote ʕamire w dukṯo hawxa basəmto w mabaḥ.
data.translation: Als ich auf die Burg hinaufstieg, waren dort lauter alte Ruinen, einige davon zerfallen, einige noch aufrechtstehende Häuser, ein gar schöner, lieblicher Platz.

rationale: New structural subsense 1b; explicit contrast between ruined and standing houses.

summary: example for sense 1b in Part act. (93/38)

data.turoyo: Aṯino annaqla l bayto, bayto hawxa yarixo, ġalabe yarixo, kibe ḥamšo w ʕəsri, əšto w ʕəsri=mətrowat, faqat hayəd qarʕe, amma u=qṭorayḏe heš šmənto kit mine, ḥaḏ̣ər, ʕamiro.
data.translation: Nun kam ich zu einem Hause, einem sehr langen Hause, etwa 25-26 Meter lang. Der Aberteil ist eingefallen, aber von der Decke steht noch ein wenig da.

rationale: Second independent structural 1b context; intact ceiling remnant cannot denote inhabitants.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (94/164)

data.turoyo: W ṭuro tamo ġalabe ʕamuro yo w i marʕa ste ġalabe ṭawto yo, mu sabab d noše lo koyotu tamo, i marʕa w u ṭuro ġalabe ṭawwe ne.
data.translation: Der Berg ist dort sehr dicht bewachsen, und die Weide ist sehr gut, weil dort keine Menschen wohnen.

rationale: Better dense-growth context: vegetation thrives precisely because people do not live there, separating density from habitation.

summary: example for sense 2 in Part act. (Jan 1.8/232)

data.turoyo: Mawbelan i Raḥel lu bayto. Qayəm aṯi l Xori Nəʕman w lu ḥasyo mbarxulle. Bəṯr 4-5, 2-3 yarḥe aṯyo ḥəlto Ḥabbo əmmo: "Alo i kalayḏan abri, ʕamərto yo!" <...>
data.translation: We brought Rachel home. Then Father Numan and the bishop came and married them. After four or five, two or three months Aunt Habbo came and said, ‘Well, our bride, my son, is pregnant!’ <...>

rationale: Only example for new Part act. sense 2; marriage and delayed announcement provide the semantic context.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (Jan 2.2/273)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: ʕAybo ʕamər bayto! Məḏyaḏ ema kowe, u mede d hawxa (gaḥxo).
data.translation: Chorepiscopus Brahim: Shame, may his house prosper! When would Midyat have something like that? (laughter)

rationale: Fourth Preterit Intransitive I.1 example; source ʕamər is kept distinct from Infectum ʕomər despite identical optative force.

summary: All 39 occurrences reviewed. I Preterit Intransitive and Infectum have optative household blessings as well as statements of habitation/revival; the person thanked is the possessor, not an overt object or builder. The formula does not establish an unexpressed divine builder.

ʕamiro/ʕamərto and ʕamuro are state predicates in the glossary's Part act. box. Plural ʕamire in 24/200 denotes settled residents; 93/33 uses the same plural shape of intact houses. Feminine ʕamə́rtowa has a past copula and is not a new finite Preterit-wa box.

The inherited sense explicitly calls for editorial revision. Its wording, including the editorial warning, is preserved. The new structural subsense clarifies an attested contrast while the inherited density examples remain in sense 1.

ʕmr 2 repeats the thanking formula and overlaps with building-state predicates. Permitted glossary lookups confirm the overlap; do not merge entire homonyms from this small input. The III Detransitive sense is supplied only to label an already present result-state example.

Exact existing 24/200, 29/372, 29/374, 35/31, 44/114, 57/77, 66/188–189, 97/45 and LB 229/Talay 1/229 passages are not added twice. Source translations remain in their edition language; no literal building gloss is substituted for free thanks translations.

Round 2, Jan Beṯ-Şawoce. English quotations below reproduce the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation. Analyses and sense distinctions rest on the Turoyo. Round-one proposals are retained as the comparison baseline and are not republished in this JSON.

The house blessing is already represented in both homonyms and round one; no new idiom or sense is proposed. Its ʕamər/ʕomər alternation is classified by surface form, not by translating both as may prosper.
ʕamərtowa and ʕamərto wa remain Part act. with a past copula. The institutional descriptions are states of occupation/activity, not evidence of a new finite building box.

The source has expressive ʕamurooooo at Jan 2.20/3808 while the reader's form field shortens it to ʕamuro. No quotation is added or normalised there; dense-growth evidence already appears in round one.

How should intact structural ʕamiro/ʕamire be divided from building ʕmr 2? In 93/38 the referent is remaining ceiling fabric, not an inhabited house.
